tables.name: companies
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE companies (
            cik TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            entity_type TEXT,
            sic TEXT,
            sic_description TEXT,
            owner_org TEXT,
            insider_transaction_for_owner_exists INTEGER,
            insider_transaction_for_issuer_exists INTEGER,
            name TEXT NOT NULL,
            ein TEXT,
            lei TEXT,
            description TEXT,
            website TEXT,
            investor_website TEXT,
            category TEXT,
            fiscal_year_end TEXT,
            state_of_incorporation TEXT,
            state_of_incorporation_description TEXT,
            phone TEXT,
            flags TEXT,
            former_names TEXT,
            created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
        )

tables.name: company_tickers
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE company_tickers (
            cik TEXT NOT NULL,
            ticker TEXT NOT NULL,
            exchange TEXT,
            PRIMARY KEY (cik, ticker),
            FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
        )

tables.name: company_addresses
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE company_addresses (
            cik TEXT NOT NULL,
            address_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- 'mailing' or 'business'
            street1 TEXT,
            street2 TEXT,
            city TEXT,
            state_or_country TEXT,
            zip_code TEXT,
            state_or_country_description TEXT,
            is_foreign_location INTEGER,
            foreign_state_territory TEXT,
            country TEXT,
            country_code TEXT,
            PRIMARY KEY (cik, address_type),
            FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
        )

tables.name: filings
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE filings (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            cik TEXT NOT NULL,
            accession_number TEXT NOT NULL,
            filing_date DATE,
            report_date DATE,
            acceptance_date_time TEXT,
            act TEXT,
            form TEXT,
            file_number TEXT,
            film_number TEXT,
            items TEXT,
            core_type TEXT,
            size INTEGER,
            is_xbrl INTEGER,
            is_inline_xbrl INTEGER,
            primary_document TEXT,
            primary_doc_description TEXT,
            created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
            UNIQUE (cik, accession_number),
            FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
        )

tables.name: table_comments

tables.name: column_comments

tables.name: column_documentation

tables.name: financial_facts
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE financial_facts (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                cik TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_value REAL,
                unit TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_category TEXT NOT NULL,
                fiscal_year INTEGER,
                fiscal_period TEXT,
                end_date DATE,
                accession_number TEXT,
                form_type TEXT,
                filed_date DATE,
                frame TEXT,
                dimension_segment TEXT,
                dimension_geography TEXT,
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)

field_guide.cik: Company identifier stored as text. Join filings using both CIK and accession number.
field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_category: Taxonomy namespace. Compare concepts only under compatible definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.fiscal_period: Source fiscal-period label. Check period length and frame for flows.
field_guide.frame: Supplementary period indicator. A missing frame does not establish annual duration.
field_guide.filed_date: Submission date, distinct from the fact period end.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.
field_guide.dimension_segment: Segment scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.
field_guide.dimension_geography: Geographic scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.

interpretation_notes: Check end_date, fiscal_period, frame and form_type before comparing flows across periods.
Check concept, unit, period length and dimensions before identifying repeats.
Repeated disclosures can reflect revisions. Retain fact IDs and accession numbers and do not sum repeats.
Do not conflate net income, parent-attributable income, operating income and pretax income.

hits.text: Now Assist for SPM, our AI solution, helps ensure that business demands, related task documentations and feedback, are communicated clearly, efficiently and effectively.

Artificial Intelligence (“AI”), particularly Generative AI (“GenAI”) and agentic AI, is driving a new wave of technology transformation. We are an early leader in applying AI to enterprise workflows and are working to remain at the forefront of AI as we continue to execute our product roadmap. As an AI platform for business transformation, the Now Platform has embedded Now Assist, our AI solution available for certain products at an additional cost, to help enhance user productivity and efficiency, thereby accelerating our customers’ return on investment in the Now Platform. For example, with Now Assist, customer service agents can solve customers’ problems quickly with AI-produced case summaries and next step suggestions; employees can obtain faster and more accurate answers using AI-powered self-service, increasing their productivity and engagement; customers can receive enhanced self-service options and improved experiences from live support agents; and developers can generate code and create apps, saving time to focus on more complex matters. We believe that with Now Assist, even customers with limited technical background can leverage AI to meaningfully contribute to their businesses’ digital transformation. Our customers have given us feedback that these enhanced products
Now Assist for LSD, our AI solution, provides practitioners with auto-generated summaries of their legal requests and matters, thereby allowing them to more easily track and manage these workstreams.

Now Assist for Security Operations, our AI solution, enhances security operations by providing AI-generated insights through automated workflows. It boosts security analysts’ productivity, accelerates issue resolution and equips chief information security officers and other security leaders with valuable insights for transforming their security operations.

App Engine can also be used in conjunction with Now Assist for Creator, our AI solution, to quickly create and scale apps on the Now Platform. Trained on code from ServiceNow engineering, results generated with Now Assist for Creator are generally higher quality and more scalable and secure than other code generation technology. This solution includes text-to-code, which converts natural language text into high-quality code suggestions, and in some cases into complete code, enabling faster development and increased productivity.

ServiceNow’s product portfolio—which spans our Technology, Customer and Industry, Employee, Creator and other Workflows—is delivered on the Now Platform. Each year, two major platform upgrades are released, delivering new standard functionality and standalone products to further simplify the way our customers work and enhance productivity. Since launching AI-powered versions of our products, we have continued to expand the Now Assist product portfolio and plan to continue to embed AI capabilities in our portfolio in the future.

Now Assist for Source-to-Pay Operations, our AI solution, delivers simple experiences that can turn conversations into requisitions, making it easy for new or occasional users to follow the right process and reduce rogue spend.

The Now Platform is uniquely positioned to bring the full potential of GenAI and agentic AI to the enterprise. With our recent software releases, we have combined the power of the Now Platform with new GenAI and agentic AI features, offered through Now Assist, to provide intelligent workflows throughout our customers’ businesses. Customers have the flexibility to tailor their AI transformation to their unique needs and expand the value of their workflows by using ServiceNow’s large language models (“LLMs”), which include models that can process different types of data, such as text, images, audio and video, and they can incorporate third-party LLMs and their own LLMs. We regularly test these models on platform-representative data to give customers confidence that the models deliver optimal performance for their intended use cases on the Now Platform. We also provide AI governance tools, including built-in monitoring and guardrails, dataset creation management and benchmarking capabilities, and visibility into adoption, usage and performance analytics. These tools are designed to allow customers to securely and responsibly build, test and deploy new use cases and applications leveraging these models. With a single data model and integrated data layer, the Now Platform enables

Now Assist for CSM, our AI solution, rapidly generates summaries for cases and chats, reduces manual work and allows agents to resolve customer issues faster. This solution helps accelerate time to resolution, reduce case volume and personalize service, which reduces the effort required by customers.

Now Assist for FSM, our AI solution, helps customers quickly summarize key takeaways for pre-work triage and job completion, minimizing time spent searching through conversation histories. It accelerates productivity by simplifying work order task summarization and knowledge generation.

Now Assist for ITOM, our AI solution, simplifies complex technical language into easy-to-understand descriptions and provides quick resolution recommendations to IT operations issues. By doing so, this solution lowers the risk of outages, enhances customer productivity and increases overall service reliability.

We had 2,109, 1,885, and 1,626 customers with ACV greater than $1 million as of December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. For purposes of customer count, a customer is defined as an entity that has a unique Dunn & Bradstreet Global Ultimate (“GULT”) Data Universal Numbering System (“DUNS”) number and an active subscription contract as of the measurement date. The DUNS number is a global standard for business identification and tracking. We make exceptions for holding companies, government entities and other organizations for which the GULT, in our judgment, does not accurately represent the ServiceNow customer. For example, while all U.S. government agencies roll up to “Government of the United States” under the GULT, we count each government agency that we contract with as a separate customer. hits.text: Renewal rate. We calculate our renewal rate by subtracting our attrition rate from 100%. Our attrition rate for a period is equal to the ACV from customers lost during the period, divided by the sum of (i) the total ACV from all customers that renewed during the period, excluding changes in price or users, and (ii) the total ACV from all customers lost during the period. Accordingly, our renewal rate is calculated based on ACV and is not based on the number of customers that have renewed. Further, our renewal rate does not reflect increased or decreased purchases from our customers to the extent such customers are not lost customers or lapsed renewals. A lost customer is a customer that did not renew an expiring contract and that, in our judgment, will not be renewed. Typically, a customer that reduces its subscription upon renewal is not considered a lost customer. However, in instances where the subscription decrease represents the majority of the customer’s ACV, we may deem the renewal as a lost customer. For our renewal rate calculation, we define a customer as an entity with a separate production instance of our service and an active subscription contract as of the measurement date, instead of an entity with a unique GULT or DUNS number. Check concept, unit, period length and dimensions before identifying repeats.
Repeated disclosures can reflect revisions. Retain fact IDs and accession numbers and do not sum repeats.
Do not conflate net income, parent-attributable income, operating income and pretax income.

sources.sql: SELECT id, fact_name, fact_value, unit, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, end_date, frame, form_type, filed_date, accession_number FROM financial_facts WHERE cik = ? AND fact_name LIKE '%Revenue%' AND unit='USD' AND fiscal_period='FY' ORDER BY end_date DESC LIMIT 40

projected_provenance.basis: Values projected by the supplied SELECT, not inferred source lineage.

message.content: I have revenue and customer-count data. Let me compute the key trends.

**ServiceNow, Inc. (CIK 1373715) — AI / Now Assist positioning and recent trend**

**Positioning (direct disclosure, FY2024 Form 10-K, period ended 2024-12-31)**
- ServiceNow describes itself as "an early leader in applying AI to enterprise workflows" and says it is "working to remain at the forefront of AI." It frames the Now Platform as "an AI platform for business transformation" with **Now Assist embedded** — its AI solution sold for certain products **at an additional cost** — to boost user productivity and accelerate customers' ROI on the platform. (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:9187)
- The company states the Now Platform "is uniquely positioned to bring the full potential of GenAI and agentic AI to the enterprise," combining the platform with new GenAI/agentic features delivered through Now Assist, with customer flexibility to use ServiceNow LLMs, third-party LLMs, or their own, plus AI governance tools (monitoring, guardrails, benchmarking). (chunk :14517)
- **Agentic AI** is offered as a Now Assist feature, letting customers create agentic skills; AI agents work alongside humans with oversight and guardrails. (chunk :10556)
- Now Assist is embedded across the portfolio — e.g., CSM, ITOM, FSM, Security Operations, SPM, Legal Service Delivery, Source-to-Pay, Creator (text-to-code), and Financial Services Operations. (chunks :23912, :18878, :24933, :21351, :22050, :30636, :35233, :32925, :25584)
- Management says it has "continued to expand the Now Assist product portfolio" since launching AI-powered product versions and "plan[s] to continue to embed AI capabilities" going forward. (chunk :11962)

**Recent trend (quantitative)**
- **Large-customer base growing:** customers with ACV > $1 million rose to **2,109 at Dec 31, 2024**, from **1,885 at Dec 31, 2023** and **1,626 at Dec 31, 2022** — +11.9% YoY in 2024 and +15.9% in 2023 (derived from disclosed counts; chunk :155333). Note the growth rate decelerated in 2024 versus 2023.
- **Revenue:** FY2024 revenue **$10,984M** vs FY2023 **$8,971M** (+22.4%, derived) and FY2022 **$7,245M** (fact IDs 1349417, 1349408, 1349396; accession 0001373715-25-000010, 10-K filed 2025-01-30).
- **Backlog:** remaining performance obligation **$22.3B at 2024-12-31** vs **$18.0B at 2023-12-31** (fact IDs 1349448, 1349444).

**Caveats / limitations**
- The bundled 10-K does **not** disclose a standalone Now Assist revenue, ACV, or customer count; AI monetization is described qualitatively (sold at additional cost, embedded in products). The ACV > $1M customer count and revenue are company-wide metrics, not AI-specific, so they indicate overall momentum rather than a direct measure of Now Assist adoption.
- The filing also flags AI-related risks: rapid AI evolution requiring significant investment, dependence on third-party infrastructure, competitors potentially incorporating AI faster, and IP risk — so the "early leader" positioning is management's characterization, not an independently verified market-share fact. (chunk :70887)
